data: with mods and the dlc's are all good and lots of fun, and also give you the best experience
Very great game, got during a steam sale and was 100% worth it, great base game and the DLC are awesome too
this is a great game, good graphics and great gameplay
Very good game, amazing graphics, good strategy
great game, lots of replayability, and different factions

At this point, I would not recommend the game at all, maybe not even on sale

I still remember when this game was announced all those years ago, I was so young, and I loved the total war franchise and you could imagine how excited I was for this game. I remember playing it around launch and experiencing some really crazy crashes and bugs, the experience was a bit disappointing and since launch I have played this game to limited capacity since.

I will say, this game has come a long way in terms of performance I believe and some of the bug fixes and patch work has definitely helped, but to me this game still just doesn't compare to the older titles. I have tried giving this game many fresh starts trying to understand and enjoy the experience, but each time I load into a battle, I see some of the same things that really made it hard to enjoy Empire and Napoleon total war.

I'm not going to go into to much detail further, but I will say that I can appreciate the attempt at seizing romes former glory, and there are some things I can still appreciate about it, but overall the experience fails to me. I think if I were going to recommend any total war game from the warscape engine era, I would highly recommend shogun 2 total war, its really well polished, and plays extremely well despite its engine.

My ninety hours with this masterpiece mostly consisted of a single co-op campaign in which I led my Macedonians to glorious conquest over the pathetic Egyptians and puny Spartan resistance (I tried diplomacy, they drew first blood)
This massive game is the ultimate nation building, army building, battle planning, politicing, back stabbing, trade route making experience out there. I will never forget when I fought back invaders from a small garrison with a force of 200 men strategically placed along the ramparts. Amazing visuals with thousands of troops on the screen at once. The sound and music will put you in the mindset needed to conquer and rule as the screams of your enemies echo throughout the world. Full single player and co-op campaigns will keep you busy for too many hours...seriously.

Fun game! Its fairly simple, but the gets more advanced and difficult the more you get in to it. Its easy enough to learn with a few trys.
Playing Rome is fun and diverse and the many factions offers different units, play styles and difficulties.
Make sure to browse the many DLCs to get even more units, factions and campaigns!
Probably the best turn based and historical game out right now, Total War 2 is goated tbh, worth my every hour

I have played all of the Total War games and I found Rome 2 to be the worst launch of them all. The game was buggy, the AI terrible and the turns took forever.
That being said, since the patches over a couple of months, the game is much better performance wise, turns zip past about as fast as other games in the series, the AI is not as bad both in battles or in its strategy on the campaign.
The graphics are really good, the battles are satisying if a little too short, and the campaign feels epic.
Of course not everybody is happy with the design choices; a lot seem to want an updated gfx engine for the first Rome game.
The developers continue to tweak the game based on community discussions, and things are going to get even better, I am sure.
I dont think many people would be disappointed with their purchase if it was released today.

loved this game... played the hell out of it so many mods! even got myself into modding stats and units + heroes only problem i've had with this game is the AI they are so stupid its unreal 98% you will need to attack them even as defenders.. when units waver chasing them off the map is annnoying seige battles are shit! i prefer to watch youtube videoes of seige battles because this game lacks to give me the satifaction

This game was a huge disappointment to anyone who has played any of the other Total war games. Here are some of the pros: Improved graphics (After all the years this should have been a given), more playable units/nations, after a few minutes I could not figure out any other pros... Here are the cons: No one can really play it on max graphics because of the horrible optimization, the game is buggy and glitchy, the combat is horrible to where it is easier just to auto resolve every battle, AI is horrible and does things that realistically would never be possible, food and happiness systems do not function correctly, sea battles are horrible, tech trees are really dumb to use, the limitations on troops which you can create until you tech up through the horrendous tech trees sucks, the loading times are rediculous, the diplomacy is broken, the combat is horrible, controlling your army has become a nightmare, probably the thing I hate the most is the unit cards where you can not even tell what the unit will remotely look like, DLC is completely an outrage because all of their DLC should have been included with the game because it does not expand the game but only allow the player to access the entire game. Overall I honestly would Never recommend this game to someone who I care the slightest for but hey, if you want to ignore all of critics about this game then be my guest.

Rome II is a Awesome fucking game. I like it for what it is, a History reflecting game with very good qualities like Puppeting States, Army Conscription, All of it is really good, I enjoyed it for when I was addicted to it, I liked it a lot, But there's a lot of stuff missing from it I won't list since this games done updating anyway, but I will say this game is really fucking good, NOT a Masterpiece but is good, I enjoyed and I heavily recommend if you like Roman Empire and shit. 7/10

Started my TW Experience with Medieval II and Rome. After playing 1k+ hours, I can state with confidence Rome II is a great game. Yes, you will need to buy quite a number of DLCs to get the full content, but I think it is worth it, because you can spend hours on end with the different civilizations/factions. If you are interested in (Roman) Antiquity and Warfare, this is one of the best games out there in my opinion.

This game is really good, graohics is better than some newer games, AI is little retarder, ngl. Anyway, Co-op mode works good, same goes to skirmish battles. Really fun, if you love historical Europe, part of Asia and Africa. I'm little sad, that you have to pay for DLC called blood and glory, that was in game for free. 8/10
awful battle balancing, combat is an uninteresting stat grind where elite units win even if they're surrounded on all sides by weaker units.

It took a min, but I can now fully recommended this game. Especially if you play with the Divide ei Impera mod. This is one of the greatest total war mods of all time, right up there with the classics like Rome Total Realism and EB, I'm not going to try and spell it, if you've been around TW Modding since Rome 1 you'll know what EB means. This is just as good as those if not better. Divide et Impera make this an easy game to recommend, but outside of the modding community the game itself is now in a recommendable state. With the inclusion of the family tree, beefed up politics, a huge living map, it feels different and nice campaigning through the various regions. Like you really went from Italy, to Greece, to Egypt, Through Africa, it's almost like getting a world tour experiencing all the rich tapestrey of Antiquity as you get to practice and try out strategies right from the all time masters like Caeser and Hannibal themselves.

If you love the Roman era, if you're a history nerd, get this game!

Total war is my favorite game series of all time. I've been a fanatic since shogun 1 when I was a child. But ever since Creative Assembly was bought by Sega, things have steadily gone down hill. They went from charging full price for a game where you could unlock all factions just by playing to charging the full price to only play as a few and then pay out the ass for DLC kindoms that have no unique units compared to those around them. Dont get me wrong, this is a good game it plays very well, Creative Assembly doesnt make bad games but look Rome II is FOUR years old now and its still 60 dollars they've put out two games since both riddled with the same full price with DLC issues. Buy this game on 50% off or don't buy it.

I struggle to say anything positive about this game. While the stability of the gameh as greatlyi ncreased, and the unit designs are very cool and seem pretty historical (unlike in the first Rome game), many steps backwards were taken, new features were half-baked if not half-arsed, some weird RPG mechanics are kind of shoved in with regards to characters, a beautiful but ultimately (and oddly at the same time) ugly and confusing UI, AI that is just as dumb if not actually worse in some ways as the AI in Rome 1 was over a decade ago and other serious issues have all combined to make lose all remaining faith I had in Creative Assembly and the Total War series. Hopefully they don't screw up their next game, but until they actualyl learn from their lessons and stop taking so many steps backwards I fear I will have to keep waiting until another developer finally brings some competition (and, in some regards, competency) to the table.

I strongly do not recommend this game, stick with the older CA games and mods. Although that said, there is, underlying it's numerous problems, an element of fun, a shadow of the glorious came that could have been and it isn't the worst game I've played (just somewhat infuriating for someone who was hoping for a hell of a lot better in this day and age from an experienced and well off developer).

Hmm, where to start on this game.

As a barebones vanilla product, this game was something that had so much potential, but came out very arcadey in the combat, and missing so many things via diplomacy.

I was severely disappointed on release, and extremely frustrated, as I missed the long, grindy, realistic battles from previous releases.

However, what this game did well, was the allowance for modders to change so much on the game, and making it available to the public.

Via mods, I have smashed out 1500 hours of this game, and still continue to play often thanks to this, and this still remains my favourite total war title to date.

TL:DR If you wish for a realistic, ancient era total war game, buy this (on special) and search steam workshop for the Divide et Impera overhaul, and tweak mods, and you will not be disappointed.

There is also a co-op mod if you wish to play with friends, which will set both of your campaign map to very hard, but leave battle map on normal (battle map difficulty above normal gives enemy units extra stats)
Pretty lit game my doods... The only thing i dont like about the game is that theres no dragons. I like dragons.... Other then that 10/10 game runs very smoothly.
Love the gameplay and the mechanics. Really compelling campaign. Just don't like that you have to buy dlc's to play online properly, even casually. It's on the border of pay to win.

This game is the epitamy of what I would call i diamond in the rough, initially it was very buggy and long turn times, but since launch CA has done a lot to update the game and honestly at this point I think its one of the better Roman war games we have for this era. I still wholeheartedly disagree with the DLC practices that CA likes to use, as I believe the game should have been complete on launch. All in all, this is a good total war game with a lot of small faults. I'd try it if you have interest in the series or the roman era. Many of the ideas introduced here like province management and the diplomacy screen would go on to influence one of my favorites in the series, Warhammer.

I started to play Total War since the very first Sugun and I really enjoy the series. Unfortunately starting from the second Rome the quality of the game dropped. I have a mac pro. I bought Rome 2 and Atilla. After a couple of hours in both games, I was no longer able to use my keyboard both on the campaign map and in the battle, which made the gameplay impossible. I tried everything and after some googling in the support forum, I realized that CA was not able to resolve this issue since 2014. It is very disappointing. After all of that my request for a refund was declined.

Grab this on sale.
It’s worth a buy, just make sure to get the blood and gore pack as well.
Loads of content.
Best enjoyed on a rainy day, or if on a COVID lockdown.

its a great strategy game for world conquest from late BC to early AD, as well as a great game to play with friends whether it be world conquest togeather or head to head or even just quick battles. you may find your self losing track of time

This game is a devourer of time. I would start up the game and then 6 hours later have no idea what the hell happened. You get so lost in trying to conquer everything, and destroying your enemies. If you have played total war games previously, you know what you are getting into. What I would say to you is, since release, the game has been patched over quite nicely and this game really shines as a result. After pushing through the main campaign on vanilla, check out the robust modding community that has created some really worthwhile mods.

For those who have never played a total war game, this is a fantastic starting place to get into the franchise and it is such a wonderful game. It has so much to offer and is extremely engrossing. I would check out some let's plays to get an idea of exactly what you are getting into, and then grab the game ON SALE. As much as I love the game I do not believe it is worth the 59.99 price tag anymore. 14.99 is a steal though. One of my favorite strategy games and it does so well immesing you in one of my favorite time periods.

Overall it is a fantastic game. And at this price, even the smallest bit of interest should be acted upon

Rome 2 released in a pretty mediocre state, but after four years and a lot of work, it's not terrible. Is it the best TW game? No, that title probably goes to Shogun 2, particularly Fall of the Samurai. Warhammer 2 is pretty sharp as well. But as far as Rome 2 goes, it's received a lot of patches and improvement aside from the DLC, and the base game is thoroughly playable and enjoyable.

Also there's Divide et Impera, which if you want a big mod to make everything slower, harder, and more complicated, there you go.

Ok like half my time in this is just being overloaded with tutorial info and needing to lay down and take a nap to let my brain simmer. 3 hours of that before I gave up on the tutorial and tried campaign for another almost 3 hours. And the tutorial voice Will. Not. Stop. Talking. ...Ever... Sometimes two voices at once. Also everything you click has a wall of text description to read. I think it explained to me in 8 different ways that units have a movement range. Truly something never heard of before in strategy games. More lay down to nap because info overload. Ready to give up on the game, I'll give historical battles a try... at least let me crush the Roman army in that ambush I watched the intro video for several times while benchmarking graphics. Nope. You can only play as Romans. Pls pls I really don't want this game, I'm much happier playing Three Kingdoms.

After such a rocky beginning, this game has made a full 180 and is now probably tied with Shogun 2 for being the best Total War available right now. The naval combat does feel worse than either Shogun 2 or Empire total war but the ambiance and game play itself is fantastic, I highly recommend mods to replace the unit cards because the original ones are pretty bad and also making each year 6 or so turns will give you a much better experience.
I can't recommend it enough.

Without doubt the best historical Total War in the franchise.
A satisfying progression of expansion and upgrading of your units in the early-to-mid campaign.
The only criticism i have to make is that conquest during the late campaign is a litlle bit boring, because you are too strong compare to your enemy and you start to autoresolve all the battle.
I give the game a 9/10.
It's a must-play if you like the franchise or if you want to experienced your first total war

Well, i tried it for the second time, for starters, i think this is really a good TOTAL WAR game, really good. but after a few days, i find it super boring myself playing as ROME, i was on Turn 80 and pretty much i am just conquering the whole world ( normal difficulty ) i don't know. battles are pretty much average, animations are not that bad, but Three kingdoms has better battle animations, the variety of units are pretty good! but the Blood and Gore DLC is super terrible though, it really makes SOME of the battle super bad in my opinion. the graphics are too cartoonish too. overall i rate it final as 6.5/10 but personally i don't really like the CAMPAIGN, especially the Diplomacy part and Politics (it felt irrelevant as time pass) but i like the Battles. if you are too obsessed with ROMAN EMPIRE history or SPARTA, or ATHENS and some MACEDONIA Military history, get this game, or if you just wanna slaughter Barbarian factions.. you will enjoy and get a good 100 hrs+ on this game, but personally its not my taste. i do still prefer Three Kingdoms and Shogun 2 as my Favorite total war games, for me its a better setting. its a personal preference after all. ( BUT IS IT A GOOD GAME AND DO I RECOMMEND IT? OFCOURSE I WOULD ) Good luck have fun all!

This game is fucking Awsome :D Yes some of it is a little buggy and unbalaced but it teaches you a lot about history and the mods are pretty damn sweet so.............Also why the hell is Wrath of spart so so hard? D: theres a weird glich where i only have 1 army vs the many armies of sparta and athens.

While not the strongest of the TOTAL WAR games, it is still fun to play. It expands on the diplomatic aspects and with the DLC adds some interesting scenarios, but it will also frustrate you, especially some of the AI enemies (and in multiplayer) that amplify the annoyance with heroes and diplomats doing far more damage than any army could ever do.

The battle tactics are pretty good, but the AI must be watched, to keep your armies intact and doing what you want them to do. Diehards to the TOTAL WAR series will want this game in their arsenal, but may prefer Rome 1; new players should probably get Rome 1 first, and get Rome 2 when they become diehards or want the bump in graphics at the cost of some game play.

Either way, wait for a sale.

6/10

This game is a fun extention of other TW games and is a good immesion into Roman history. The story missions are fun and a lot of campaigns are interesting to learn about and play out/change history. Decent gameplay but not a lot of deep engagement or return to play desire.

I found that the mechanics of this TW game was pretty slow. I felt I couldnt move my units to flank others quickly, and that cavalry and ranged units were largely ineffective. Most engagements/skirmishes become a mash of slowly dying units that feels ultimatley out of your control.

The Seige/Battle commands are improved and campaign movement/recruitment is a good addition to the TW series. That being said Ill Take Empire/Napoleon/Shogun 2 over Rome II.

Enjoyable game, however DLC should not be ripping existing factions and putting them on a price tag. True DLC is adding extended content such as the Caesar in Gaul Campaign, thats what DLC's should be. Also the game price is a bit high for being over 5 years old, atleast cut the price in half.

I love the game but I havent been able to play it for months. It wont launch anymore, I click play and it says it is syncing but the lauch fails. I have tried everything but with no success. Absolutely furious given how much it costs in total with all the DLC.
I have been given no support or help on how to fix it either even though I have seen many people post with the same issue.
No matter how good the game is, I cant recommend if it is unplayable!!

Total War Rome 2 doesn't bring distaste as it is a beautiful delicate rose of fine tuned machinery sure to put you with great views of scenic battles from long past, as you march and build your armies you begin to feel as if you truly are the emperor or senate. fw this game heavy #hollahforadollah.

Total war: ROME II has been vastly improved from last years catastrophic release. This is the game that should have been released originally. It's not perfect but it's now a solid fun TW Rome experience, which I can finally comfortably recommend.
At first I heard pretty bad things about this game but 5 hours in its pretty good, historical tactics worked great, and custom battles were very fun.
Brilliant game. Enjoyable variations in factions and play-styles. The games AI isn't the smartest but can still surprise you from time to time. Easily one of the best of the Total War series to date.

On today's PCs this vast game runs extremely smoothly and with its various Graphics updates over the years it still deserves a place in your Games Library

The Grand Campaign is an absolute Epic. It also takes a VERY Long time to play til the end
For me, this is what Total War is all about *****

even though i took some time away from this gamer (laptop acting up) i was finally able to come back to it, my love for Greek and Roman history really connected me to this game. It's really fun to play with both historical battles and a campain where to can make your own history. heard tell of a Spartacus DLC somewhere if so please can someone let me know as Spartacus is one of my fav parts of Roman history.

Rome 2 is an all time favorite of mine. The amount of hours this game can provide is astounding.

I can't play the game without the DEI mod, so go check that out!
Really fun, enjoy it a lot. This was one of the first total war games I played and have all the DLC for too

Even though heavily criticised at launch, this has always been one of my favourite Total War games and it has only got better over the years, with long standing support from Creative Assembly - well worth it, particularly as it is now quite old and is often on sale.
A truly amazing experience. Sadly, I only got to play it 11 years after release, but it was totally worth it. A lot of replay value!

This is a absolute gem of a game. A great Total War Experience. The time period is great and having so many unique peoples to play as, adds great variety. I would recommend this game to history and military fans.
Emporer Edition really fixed a lot of issues the game had upon release. Even with its few remaining flaws, this is an extremly fun game that you can easily sink over 100 into.

I play almost exclusively with mods for this game. DEI mod has brought my love back to the game after years away. while the AI is not good. I handicap myself by playing as "realistic" as possible. move the armies how i think the character's leading them would and all that. Its a game where you can create your own narrative for the ups and downs of your civilization. Have fun with the large variety of units.
overall it is a fun game that is filled with bugs which are more apparent the more you play. however it is still one of my favourites.

reason.text: Negative reviews focus on a buggy game state at launch, and several say that even after patching the problems remained.
Reviews also object to simplified systems and paid DLC, and a news headline from the same month covers the first expansion announcement.
